messages.content:
Risk: Excessive Agency
Description: An LLM-based system is often granted a degree of agency by its developer - the ability to call functions or interface with other systems via extensions (sometimes referred to as tools, skills or plugins by different vendors) to undertake actions in response to a prompt. The decision over which extension to invoke may also be delegated to an LLM 'agent' to dynamically determine based on input prompt or LLM output. Agent-based systems will typically make repeated calls to an LLM using output from previous invocations to ground and direct subsequent invocations. Excessive Agency is the vulnerability that enables damaging actions to be performed in response to unexpected, ambiguous or manipulated outputs from an LLM, regardless of what is causing the LLM to malfunction.
Concern: None
Policy: Operational Security & Critical Infrastructure

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/GoalsAndObjectives/Objectives/Aim: aim — intention specifying a desired direction, condition, or situation toward which an agent's actions are directed, without requiring precise scope or measurable criteria [found by 5/6 queries]
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 6/6 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/Authorization: authorisation — situation in which a party authorizes someone to act on their behalf or to have specific capabilities under certain conditions for some period of time [found by 6/6 queries]
  Siblings: trade, ownership control situation, study
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#AlgorithmicDiscrimination: Algorithmic Discrimination — Systematic bias in automated decision-making systems that disadvantages specific groups based on protected characteristics. [found by 5/6 queries]
  Siblings: Employment Discrimination, Discriminatory Denial of Service, Housing Discrimination
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Organizations/Capability: capability — ability to perform a specific function or achieve a particular outcome [found by 5/6 queries]
  Siblings: index value, classifier, value
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizingParty: authorising party — party that delegates some role, authority, or control to another party [from restriction: hasAuthorizingParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: owner, registrar, controlling party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizedParty: authorised party — party that has been given the ability to act on behalf of another party or to have specified capabilities under some set of guidelines for some period of time [from restriction: hasAuthorizedParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: Occupation Role, Contractor Role, service provider

axes.rationale: The risk involves an LLM-based system acting as an agent, making decisions and taking actions based on prompts. This class directly represents the 'agent' performing the actions.
The risk describes the system being granted the ability to act, which is a form of authorization. This class represents the means by which the agent is allowed to perform actions.
